title_as_printed: Enthalpy of Solution of Hydrocarbon Gases into Water at 25 C and Atmospheric Pressure
pressure_note: partial pressure of the gas p_G in kPa (footnote d); title says 'atmospheric pressure'; total minus water vapour pressure per text of the paper

value.what: heat of solution under experimental conditions (Eq. 1 dH_sol). Printed values are positive (e.g. 13.289 for methane) whereas Table II lists the standard values as negative (-13.18), so the printed number is treated as heat evolved (-dH); scale -1 is an inference from comparison with Table II and should be checked in pass 2

extra.what: steady-state thermopile voltage (volts), printed as 10^6 E

composition.other_species: pure water; water flow rate printed in each block label

extra_unmapped: water flow rate in block label
notes: Exponent in each block label: methane/ethane/propane/butane/2-methylpropane/2,2-dimethylpropane 2.7e-8 m3/s; cyclopropane 8.7e-9; ethene 6.9e-9; propene 7.3e-9; 1-butene 7.4e-9; ethyne 8.8e-9. The block labelled 'Butane' is n-butane per the experimental section (listed gases). Blocks have per-trial rows with the printed +- value attached to the voltage cell, written as a separate '+- E' column (printed '+-' sign omitted). Propane trial 5 p_G = 83.53 as printed (others 86.1-86.9, likely misprint, kept).
